title: Stacked guarded levels are not inlined into a 2^k tree
verdict: plan and run stay small at 40 levels
description: Forty stacked projections, each appending a reach and a guarded column that read the previous reach twice (so an optimizer that merges projections by substitution would build a tree of 2^40 copies), plan and run in well under a second of engine time and under 100 MB of extra memory. Optimized plan text by levels (5, 10, 20, 40): 2,377, 6,266, 17,724 and 55,044 characters (`LazyFrame.explain()`); planning 3 ms to 7 ms; running 4 ms to 11 ms; process peak 38 MB to 44 MB. The text grows about quadratically, not exponentially, for the same reason. The result matches the reference at every level.
reference: No reference counterpart: the reference has no plan size. D50-d needs the plan of a chain of k guarded levels to cost time and memory linear in k.

evidence.note: `python -m sverify_dev.guarded_columns p2 --engine polars`: Polars 2.1.0 (Python), streaming engine, Linux x86_64 (homelab); the P1 cases also ran on macOS arm64 for DuckDB and Polars with the same result.

provenance.notes: Issue #1719 (D50-d). Probe rows: 3000, every third one the text `bad`, which a strict cast rejects.
